claims.text: The proposed material is the refractory high-entropy alloy Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr.
This alloy can exhibit a ductile–brittle–ductile transition as temperature increases.
Condition (1) processing produces a continuous ordered B2 matrix with discrete BCC precipitates.
The continuous ordered B2-matrix condition is brittle at room temperature.
Condition (1) has a yield strength of 2032 MPa and a compressive fracture strain of 4.7%.
Condition (2) produces a single-phase weakly ordered BCC structure containing nanometer-scale B2 regions.
Condition (2) has greater than 60% compressive ductility and a yield strength of 1065 MPa.

The proposed treatment consists of casting, hot isostatic pressing at 1200 °C, homogenization at 1200 °C, solution treatment at 1400 °C followed by water quenching, and annealing at 600 °C followed by water quenching.
The 600 °C annealing step is conducted for 120 hours.
Condition (3) produces an inverted microstructure consisting of a continuous disordered BCC matrix and discrete B2 precipitates.
The discrete B2 precipitates in Condition (3) are approximately 50 nm in size.
The continuous disordered BCC matrix facilitates dislocation mobility and thereby provides room-temperature ductility.
The discrete B2 precipitates provide precipitation strengthening.
The inverted-microstructure alloy has high ductility and good or moderate strength at room temperature.
At approximately 600 °C, the inverted-microstructure alloy exhibits anomalous strengthening and elevated yield strength.
At approximately 600 °C, the inverted-microstructure alloy suffers a reduction in ductility corresponding to a brittle-like state.
Dislocation interactions with B2 precipitates, competing slip systems, and localized impediment of dislocation motion cause the proposed intermediate-temperature strengthening and ductility loss.
At temperatures above 600 °C, thermal activation overcomes the barriers to dislocation motion and restores ductility.
The cited study conducted uniaxial compression tests at 25 °C and 600 °C using an initial strain rate of 0.001 s−1.
Similar refractory high-entropy alloys with an inverted BCC-matrix/B2-precipitate microstructure are also expected to show this transition.
